summary: Media/stream facts for a Windows Tapo client. RTSP (:554 /stream1,/stream2) and ONVIF (:2020) are camera-firmware services; the app only manages the 'Camera Account' (user_management/third_account) and RTSP/ONVIF security config, so RTSP URI patterns are external knowledge. The app's own LOCAL media transport is an HTTP/1.1 long-lived POST to /stream on port 8800 (plain TCP, HTTP Digest auth, per-part AES-128-CBC) or port 28800 (TLS-PSK, no digest), with multipart/mixed framing using boundary '--client-stream-boundary--'. Video arrives as MPEG-TS parts (video/mp2t); control is JSON parts {type:request|response|notification, seq, params}. Talkback uses the same /stream endpoint with a 'talk' request and uploads audio/mp2t parts (default G.711 A-law 8 kHz).

items.description: App's own local LAN media endpoint (connection type CONNECTION_LOCAL=256). Port 28800 is used when the device advertises a TLS-PSK local_stream_type; otherwise 8800 plain TCP. Path is /stream plus an optional query suffix built from StreamUriParams.

value.query_note: query suffix is only set when StreamUriParams is provided (relay/new flows); plain '/stream' works for local preview (pytapo)

items.description: HTTP Digest challenge/response on the persistent socket, then the same socket stays open as a bidirectional multipart stream.

value.step1_request:
POST /stream HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=--client-stream-boundary--
User-Agent: <http.agent>
Host: <ip>:<port>
Connection: Keep-Alive
Accept-Encoding: gzip
Content-Length: 0
X-Key-Exchange: 1
value.step1_response: HTTP/1.1 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Digest realm=..., qop="auth", nonce=..., opaque=..., algorithm=MD5|SHA-256, [encrypt_type=3], [salt=...], [userhash=true], [charset]
value.step2_request: POST /stream HTTP/1.1 with headers in order: Content-Type (multipart/mixed; boundary=--client-stream-boundary--), Authorization: Digest ..., User-Agent, Connection: keep-alive, Content-Length: 0, X-Key-Exchange: 1 (omitted on TLS-PSK socket)
value.step2_response: HTTP/1.1 200 (or 204) with header Key-Exchange: username="admin" nonce="<hex>" [cipher=..] [padding=..] [algorithm=HKDF] [salt=..]; body may contain JSON with session_id
value.after_200: client immediately sends JSON control part (e.g. preview request) and then reads parts until closed
value.x_key_exchange_rule: X-Key-Exchange: 1 is sent only when the socket is NOT TLS-PSK
value.tls_psk_rule: on port 28800 with TLS 1.2/1.3 PSK the digest step is skipped (f186141r=true => K() false)

error_codes.503: device busy; body JSON has error_code (e.g. -52407 too many clients)

items.description: RFC 2617/7616-style Digest computed by the app (sb1.g).

value.password_input: TP-Link cloud account password (plaintext from logged-in account); fallback default 'TPL075526460603' if empty; NVR channels use NVR password
value.hash_alg: algorithm param from challenge: SHA-256 if given, else MD5; '-sess' suffix stripped for hashing
value.cnonce: 16 chars alternating random lowercase letter / digit; fallback 'a9h5b7i3j2y8c0a6'
value.userhash: if challenge userhash=true then username := H(username:realm) and userhash=true

items.description: Legacy per-part media encryption key derivation from the Key-Exchange response header (when Key-Exchange has no algorithm=HKDF).

value.key_exchange_parse: split header value on ' '; each token k=v; strip double quotes; required key 'nonce'; optional username, cipher, padding, algorithm, salt
value.password: the transformed password used for digest (UPPERCASE_HEX MD5 or SHA256 of cloud password)
value.username_rule: if username == 'admin' (GenKey default username) use the transformed user password; if username == 'none' use default password 'TPL075526460603' (untransformed); otherwise no decryption (unknown username)
value.per_part: each encrypted multipart body is decrypted independently with Cipher.doFinal (IV resets to the fixed IV for every part)

items.description: Newer key schedule when Key-Exchange contains algorithm=HKDF and salt. Per-part IV comes from the X-Nonce header (hex); parts are authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 (encrypt-then-MAC).

value.hkdf: HKDF-SHA256 (BouncyCastle HKDFBytesGenerator, SHA-256 digest), salt = Key-Exchange 'salt' (UTF-8 bytes), L = 16
value.aes_iv: hex-decode(X-Nonce header of the part); new cipher per X-Nonce
value.integrity_failure: part dropped; if failures persist > 5 s => error -2001 'integrity checks continue to fail'
value.upload: client-generated 16 random bytes hex as X-Nonce for each uploaded (talk) part; X-Data-Hmac computed over the encrypted bytes

items.description: Multipart framing in both directions on the persistent socket. Client parts begin with '----client-stream-boundary--' (i.e. '--' + boundary), device parts with '----device-stream-boundary--'. Each part = boundary line, headers, blank line, Content-Length bytes, CRLF.

value.parser_rule: line containing '--device-stream-boundary--' starts a part; HTTP status line also parsed; Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies are not read by Content-Length
